value.notes: Controlled selection. RadioGroup is generic: <RadioGroup<'ssd' | 'hdd'> value=... /> is documented usage.

name.notes: Identifies the field for form submission.

dataAttributes: data-disabled — present when the group is disabled
data-valid/data-invalid, data-dirty/data-touched, data-filled, data-focused — Field.Root state

renderProp.elementForm: <Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup<'ssd'|'hdd'> defaultValue="ssd" />}> is the documented composition for a labelled group

formIntegration.hiddenInput: Renders the hidden radio inputs for the group members; name on RadioGroup is what the form sees.
formIntegration.validation: required is enforced; renders role="radiogroup" with aria-required/aria-disabled/aria-readonly.

keyboard.keys: Roving focus over the radios via internals/composite: ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, Home, End; loopFocus defaults to true (wrap-around at the ends).
keyboard.focus: Single tab stop for the whole group.

notableDifferences: React Aria's RadioGroup exposes orientation + isReadOnly/isRequired/isInvalid; Base UI exposes disabled/readOnly/required and no orientation prop.
The group's value is generic over Value, so a typed union migrates cleanly (React Aria is string-based Key).
Labelling the group requires aria-labelledby or composing with Fieldset.Root — there is no Label part on RadioGroup itself.
Disabled/readOnly/required propagate from the group down to the radios; in React Aria these are per-Radio too.
